Kaavakuva: viisi tapaa tuottaa sähköä. P: Schematic diagram: five ways of producing electricity. Falling water turns a water turbine and wind turns a rotor, and the shaft of each turns a generator G. Solar radiation hits a solar panel, which produces electricity directly without a generator. The nuclear energy of uranium heats steam in a reactor and the chemical energy of fuel heats steam in a boiler, and the steam turns a turbine and a generator. The grey arrows are the energy of the natural resource, the dark arrows are electricity, and from every plant an orange arrow points downwards: some of the energy ends up as heat in the surroundings. The figure is schematic; the length of the arrows does not show power.
Vaakapylväskaavio Suomen sähköntuotannos: Horizontal bar chart of electricity production in Finland in 2024 by energy source in terawatt-hours (Statistics Finland), to scale: nuclear power 31, wind power 20.2, hydropower 14.1, biofuels 9.5, fossil fuels and peat 3.4 and solar power 0.9. The bar for nuclear power is about two fifths of the total production of 79.9.
Pistekuvaaja yksittäisten voimalaitosten: Dot plot of the powers of individual power plants on a logarithmic scale, where each vertical line is ten times the previous one: solar panels of a detached house about 5 kW, wind turbine about 5 MW, large hydropower plant about 100 MW and Olkiluoto 3 about 1600 MW. The position of a point shows the power of ten of the power, so Olkiluoto 3 is about 320 times larger than a wind turbine, although its point is only two and a half steps further to the right.
